A.  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK EQUESTRIAN CENTER STRUCTURES BID RESULTS

 8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

A.  CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING – ORDINANCE NO. 713 FOR SECOND
  READING AND ADOPTION; PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 20-16; APPLICANT:
  JUDY CHAI; LOCATION: 5883 CREST ROAD

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO ADOPT ORDINANCE 713 AMENDING THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  ZONING MAP – REZONING FROM COMMERCIAL LIMITED DISTRICT TO
  MEDIUM DENSITY RESIDENTIAL DISTRICT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 33-16; LOCATION: 4 SILVER SADDLE LANE;
  APPLICANT: TODD FANADY (AMECO SOLAR) ON BEHALF OF MORLEY AND
  ERIKA MENDELSON

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the public hearing; 2) Take
  public testimony; 3) Discuss the issues; 4) Close the public hearing; and 5)
  Direct staff to prepare a Resolution denying PA-33-16.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN inquired as to how many variances are presently on this
  property. Senior Planner Naughton noted that one was approved in 1989
  connecting the detached garage to a portion of the breezeway to create a five car
  garage.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN inquired if there are any current code violations on this
  property and if any code enforcement had taken place. Planning Director
  Wahba noted the following violations: 1) Pool fencing; 2) Gate across the
  driveway; and 3)  Carport, with no action being taken with respect to
  enforcement.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF referred to the roof commenting that the cost to install
  solar panels would be exorbitant. Planning Director Wahba noted that their
  Cal-shake roof is not suitable for solar panels and the entire roof would have to
  be replaced to accommodate the panels.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF noted that before the Planning Commission heard this
  case, staff recommended denial due to the fact that the location proposed for
  the panels is by code definition their front yard, but MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF
  noted that it actually functions as their backyard because of the way the lot
  was originally developed.

  City Manager Prichard asked that Planning Director Wahba clarify the location
  between the house and street. While doing so, Planning Director Wahba then
  explained that the shrubbery height is also not to code.

  Senior Planner Naughton responded to several questions posed by the
  COUNCIL.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF

  TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MARCH 28, 2017
   Morley Mendelson, Applicant, inquired if any of the COUNCIL visited the site
  and explained the reasons for the alleged code violations and explained how the
  property was developed over time.

  Mr. Mendelson then referred to another neighbor’s addition which was
  permitted by the City even though that front yard setback is less than the
  setback on his property. He further noted that he was encouraged to appeal
  the denial to the COUNCIL.

  Erika Mendelson, Applicant, commented that if this was on the roof, it would be
  an eyesore to the neighbors so they planned to install the solar panels in a
  location where they could not be seen.

  Jill Felts, 31 Ranchview Road, commented that she went by the property to see
  what was being proposed. She noted that looking up the hillside you cannot
  tell where the panels would be located and suggested the COUNCIL visit the
  site.

  Mrs. Felts also mentioned that the Applicants have not trimmed their trees in
  years, and they are obstructing her view. She commented that she was not
  pleased and that the Applicants are not being friendly to their neighbors.

  Liz Lewin, 29 Ranchview Road, commented that her home borders the
  Applicant’s and asked if a “frame” could be provided to determine if there would
  be an obstruction and see how this would affect the neighborhood.

  Mr. Mendelson responded to Mrs. Felts commenting that he is willing to trim
  the trees and restore the neighbors’ views. He then invited the neighbors to go
  by and see the location for themselves.

  Stephen Lai, Palos Verdes Lane, commented that looking up towards the
  property you can see the top of the Applicant’s fence, and if the panels are
  installed below the fence, they would not be seen.

  Tom Felts, 31 Ranchview Road, asked if the solar panels would be in a fixed
  position or rotate. Planning Director Wahba responded that they would be
  fixed.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that there has been discussion regarding
  aesthetics which is not the issue. She further noted that the legal analysis is
  the question and a finding for a variance could not be made by the Planning
  Commission. She then acknowledged that installing the panels on the roof is
  very expensive and the front yard is less expensive, but because the cost is less
  is not a reason to grant a variance.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN concurred with COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL’S comments
  regarding the legal issue. He noted that the City has a right to regulate health
  and safety and use its land use authority and that setbacks are required for
  first responders accessing the neighborhood in the event of an emergency. He
  concurred that aesthetics is not the main issue and that the question is the
  allowing of structures in the front yard.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that while the Applicant does make a point in
  that the panels cannot be seen, his concern is setting a precedent by allowing a
  structure in the front yard as defined by the code with no access for emergency
  situations.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MARCH 28, 2017
   MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF commented that she believes there are enough
  questions in this case, and it seems that the property owners have struggled
  over the years with how their home is angled. She further noted that the legal
  application is too narrow and would like to see more creativity in how to
  address this application. Finally she noted that the COUNCIL should be flexible
  in this situation because it is unique.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN stated that the code is clear and cannot be ignored. He
  then asked if there is a way to make appropriate findings for a variance and
  have staff and the City Attorney participate in finding a solution.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that the aerial view is restricted and referred
  to a picture of the neighborhood and believed the issue is not the front or
  backyard, but rather the street facing the yard. He further noted that the yard
  itself is a street facing yard and that he is sympathetic to the Applicant because
  the neighbors agree with this panel application and the City does encourage
  solar power installation. His question is whether or not to strictly comply with
  the fact that a separate structure cannot be in the front yard. Finally he stated
  that some of the neighboring homes are much closer to the street than the
  Applicant’s.

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN Planning Director Wahba
  responded that if the non-compliant vegetation and fence were removed, the
  panels would be seen from public view.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL stated that perhaps the property is considered
  unique in that the front and back yards are essentially reversed.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that a number of homes in the area have
  variances and stated other instances where homes have reversed yards.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL asked if variances were granted for those homes.
  Planning Director Wahba stated that there were variances granted, but no one
  has solar panels in their front yard.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, Planning Director Wahba noted that
  every application would have to be considered on a case-by-case basis.

  City Attorney Davis noted that the fact finding questions are in the staff report
  and certain standards and conditions need to be met to consider this
  application unique.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN concurred that the property is unique and
  commented that the Planning Commission and staff did a great job on this to
  make sure the code is followed. He further noted that the COUNCIL has some
  discretion in determining the outcome of this application and is inclined to
  grant this request upon appropriate findings.

  City Attorney Davis noted that every property is unique and that findings may
  be able to be made. He cautioned about the effect this might have on future
  applications.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL recommended continuing this item to allow the
  COUNCIL to visit the site.

  City Attorney Davis noted that it may be helpful to know how many properties
  are similar to the Applicant’s. He then referred to the comment about the City
  not having a policy regarding solar panels and emphasized that the COUNCIL is
  open to solar panels and it is not a question of ground-mounted versus rooftop
  installations, but that this is an issue of front yard location.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that if conditions are imposed for the
  screening, there needs to be ongoing enforcement by the City to make sure that
  the landscaping is maintained.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that the trees shielding the panels are well
  below the view corridor.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
MARCH 28, 2017
   City Manager Prichard referred to the vegetation and noted that the code allows
  two feet or less for a hedge and the existing hedge is six feet tall. He noted that
  if the COUNCIL wishes to allow for a variance based upon maintenance of the
  front yard landscaping, the COUNCIL would be acknowledging and conditioning
  a code violation.

  In response to City Manager Prichard, Planning Director Wahba noted that the
  setback requirements are there to preserve open space in the front yard to
  benefit the general public.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO CONTINUE THE PUBLIC HEARING TO A FUTURE MEETING TO
  ALLOW THE COUNCIL TO VISIT THE APPLICANT’S PROPERTY FOR
  FURTHER DISCUSSION AND DIRECT STAFF TO IDENTIFY SIMILARLY
  SITUATED PROPERTIES AND DIRECTED STAFF TO LIST THE EXISTING
  CODE VIOLATIONS ON THIS PROPERTY.

  City Manager Prichard noted that all five COUNCIL MEMBERS will be in
  attendance at the meetings of April 25 and May 9.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted his concern with approving an application when
  there are still code violations. He further noted his desire to study this more
  carefully and consider how those code issues would be resolved to bring them
  into compliance. Finally he stated that he wants to make sure the City abides
  by its laws and to limit the potential of this issue getting out of hand and not
  create future problems.

  City Manager Prichard noted that the the public hearing will be re-noticed for a
  future meeting.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.
